articles.title: Enfermeira que matou os 3 filhos: júri não alcança unanimidade  | G1
articles.standfirst: Defesa tenta convencer os jurados de que Lindsay Clancy sofria de psicose pós-parto. Já a Promotoria tem o ônus de provar que ela era responsável por seus atos no momento dos assassinatos.
articles.summary: Os jurados do julgamento de Lindsay Clancy, a enfermeira dos EUA que matou os três filhos, informaram o juiz nesta terça-feira (1º)  que não conseguem chegar a uma decisão unânime.
articles.body:
Lindsay Clancy durante seu julgamento por homicídio — Foto: David L. Ryan/The Boston Globe via AP, Pool

Os jurados do julgamento de Lindsay Clancy, a enfermeira dos EUA que matou os três filhos , informaram o juiz nesta terça-feira (1º) que não conseguem chegar a uma decisão unânime sobre a condenação de Clancy.

➡️ Em um caso que chocou e dividiu os Estados Unidos , a enfermeira é julgada por homicídio após ter matado seus três filhos pequenos em casa em 2023 por estrangulamento . A defesa alega que ela sofria de psicose pós-parto.

Apesar do impasse no júri, o juiz William Sullivan, do Tribunal Superior de Plymouth, instruiu os jurados a prosseguirem até que consigam encontrar um veredicto final. As deliberações do júri entraram no quarto dia nesta terça. O julgamento começou há cerca de dois meses.

Ao lado de seu advogado, Lindsay Clancy, acusada de homicídio por matar os três filhos, olha ao júri durante julgamento de seu caso, em 1º de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Greg Derr/ Pool via Reuters

Três anos após as mortes, o julgamento se concentra no estado mental de Lindsay Clancy no momento do crime. A defesa tenta convencer os jurados de que ela sofria de psicose pós-parto, um transtorno psiquiátrico raro associado ao estresse, à privação de sono e às alterações hormonais após o parto.

Já a Promotoria afirma que Clancy, ex-enfermeira obstétrica, matou intencionalmente os filhos Dawson, de 3 anos, Cora, de 5, e Callan, de 8 meses, em janeiro de 2023, e deve ser responsabilizada criminalmente pelas mortes.

O julgamento também tem impulsionado nos EUA a discussão sobre psicose e outros transtornos pós-parto, e grupos de mulheres se manifestaram do lado de fora da corte na semana passada a favor de Clancy e defendendo mais atenção à saúde mental das mulheres .

Os jurados têm cinco opções para o desfecho do caso. Veja, a seguir, o que cada uma das alternativas significa para a ré:

A própria defesa de Clancy não nega que Clancy tenha asfixiado seus três filhos com faixas elásticas para exercício. Por isso, é improvável que ela seja considerada inocente pura e simples, sem menção à alegação de insanidade mental (leia mais abaixo) .

No entanto, a lei de Massachusetts, onde o caso está sendo julgado, não coloca o ônus da prova do lado da ré: é a Promotoria que precisa provar, para além de qualquer dúvida razoável, que ela era responsável por seus atos no momento em que os assassinatos ocorreram .

Inocente por motivo de insanidade mental

Os jurados podem considerar Clancy inocente caso cheguem à conclusão de que, mesmo tendo matado seus filhos, ela sofria de psicose pós-parto que a tornava incapaz de ser responsabilizada por seus atos. Essa é a tese da defesa.

Caso ela seja considerada inocente por falta de responsabilidade criminal, como em caso de insanidade mental, a lei estadual permite que a corte determine sua internação compulsória para tratamento.

No direito americano, a condenação por assassinato em primeiro grau significa dizer que o ato foi intencional e premeditado — ou, ainda, cometido com extrema crueldade.

Essa é o pior desfecho para Clancy, já que a lei de Massachusetts determina, nesses casos, que a condenação seja invariavelmente a prisão perpétua sem possibilidade de condicional.

No código penal estadual, essa classificação se aplica a um homicídio cometido com intenção ou extrema imprudência, mas sem planejamento prévio. Neste caso, a ré será condenada à prisão perpétua, porém com possibilidade de condicional.

O júri pode considerar ainda que ela cometeu o crime, mas que os assassinatos foram resultados de uma "conduta temerária ou imprudente".

A principal diferença para o homicídio doloso é a intenção. É um desfecho possível para Clancy caso os jurados sejam convencidos de que os assassinados ocorreram sem planejamento, mas que a decisão de cometer o ato tenha sido impulsiva.

Nesse caso, a Promotoria não precisa provar que ela tinha a intenção de causar a morte dos filhos.

articles.title: Leonardo DiCaprio faz visita restrita ao Cacique Raoni em MT  | G1
articles.standfirst: Atualmente, o líder indígena está acamado e se recupera na região do Xingu, ao lado de familiares e amigos.
articles.summary: Atualmente, o líder indígena está acamado e se recupera na região do Xingu, ao lado de familiares e amigos.
articles.body:
Leonardo DiCaprio visita Cacique Raoni no Alto Xingu — Foto: Reprodução

A visita do ator norte-americano Leonardo DiCaprio ao Raoni Metuktire, de 94 anos, no último sábado (29), foi restrita , com a participação de poucas pessoas, conforme familiares do cacique ouvidos pelo g1 . O encontro acontece pouco mais de um mês da alta hospitalar do cacique, que chegou a ser transferido de avião do Hospital Dois Pinheiros , em Sinop , para o Hospital São Paulo.

🔍O líder indígena é uma das vozes mais influentes do Brasil na defesa dos indígenas e do meio ambiente. Ele iniciou seu ativismo em 1954, aprendeu português, e foi uma voz importante para o reconhecimento dos direitos dos povos indígenas na Constituição de 1988.

O cacique ficou mundialmente conhecido após encontros com famosos. Atualmente, o líder indígena está acamado e se recupera na região do Xingu , ao lado de familiares e amigos.

DiCaprio está em viagem no Pantanal e decidiu fazer uma parada Parque Indígena do Xingu, onde Raoni se recupera. O teor da conversa não foi divulgado.

Leonardo DiCaprio e Gisele Bündchen durante visita ao Parque Indígena do Xingu, em 2004 — Foto: Reprodução

Esta não foi a primeira vez que Leonardo DiCaprio esteve na região. Em 2004, o ator visitou o Xingu acompanhado da então modelo Gisele Bündchen, com quem mantinha um relacionamento na época. Além de ator, DiCaprio também é ativista ambiental e possui um longo histórico de envolvimento e financiamento de pautas ligadas ao meio ambiente e à conservação global.

Ao longo de décadas de atuação em defesa dos povos indígenas, Raoni se encontrou com diversas personalidades, incluindo artistas, autoridades e líderes religiosos.

Em 2025, o cacique recebeu a atriz norte-americana Angelina Jolie, que visitou a aldeia Piaraçu, na Terra Indígena Capoto-Jarina, na região do Xingu.

A atriz Angelina Jolie e o cacique Raoni — Foto: Mauricio Dias

No ano anterior, em 2024, Raoni esteve com o papa Francisco no Vaticano , em Roma. Durante o encontro, entregou ao pontífice uma carta na qual abordava as mudanças climáticas e os impactos de eventos extremos no Brasil.

O cacique Raoni Metuktire, líder do povo Kayapó, entregou uma carta ao Papa Francisco — Foto: Divulgação Vaticano

O cacique também já se encontrou com a cantora Anitta e o apresentador Luciano Huck . Durante o encontro, foram discutidos assuntos como os direitos dos povos indígenas e a Conferência das Partes (COP), realizada em Belém (PA).

Anitta e Luciano Huck visitam cacique Raoni em MT — Foto: Reprodução

No dia 15 de junho, Raoni foi internado na UTI do Hospital Dois Pinheiros, em Sinop (MT), após passal mal na aldeia onde morava. Os exames iniciais apontaram alterações na função renal e indicadores compatíveis com um processo infeccioso grave. A principal hipótese diagnóstica foi sepse com foco pulmonar, conforme o hospital.

Um mês antes, ele foi internado no mesmo hospital após sentir fortes dores na barriga devido à uma hernia antiga, mas recebeu alta médica após dois dias de tratamento. Cinco dias depois, Raoni voltou a apresentar complicações de saúde e foi novamente para a UTI para tratar um quadro de pneumonia, onde permaneceu por mais sete dias.

Segundo a unidade de saúde, o líder indígena apresentava múltiplas comorbidades, entre elas Doença Pulmonar Obstrutiva Crônica (DPOC), cardiopatia com marcapasso implantado e insuficiência cardíaca.

Em setembro de 2022, ele chegou a ficar internado por cinco dias no hospital de Sinop, após ser diagnosticado com um problema cardíaco e passar por cirurgia para implante de marcapasso. Depois, passou alguns dias no município de Colíder até voltar para a aldeia.

Além disso, em julho de 2020, o cacique foi internado em um hospital de Colíder após ter passado mal. Ele chegou a ser transferido de avião para Sinop com complicações gastrointestinais e desidratação.

Em setembro do mesmo ano, foi novamente internado com diagnóstico de pneumonia pela equipe médica de sua aldeia, no Parque Indígena do Xingu. À época, recebeu alta médica nove dias depois. Ainda neste período, também apresentou um quadro depressivo após a morte da mulher dele, Bekwyjkà Metuktire.

articles.title: Vice-presidente do Bank of América morre após facada na Times Square | G1
articles.standfirst: Erin Piacenti, vice-presidente do banco, morreu após ser atingida por facada. Criminosa esfaqueou Piacenti, de 32 anos, e outro homem. Depois, foi morta por policiais.
articles.summary: A vítima do esfaqueamento na quinta-feira (31) na Times Square, em Nova York, nos Estados Unidos, foi identificada como a vice-presidente do Bank of America Erin Piacenti.
articles.body:
A vítima do esfaqueamento na quinta-feira (31) na Times Square, em Nova York, nos Estados Unidos , foi identificada como a vice-presidente do Bank of America Erin Piacenti. Piacenti, de 32 anos, foi uma das duas pessoas esfaqueadas por uma mulher, que depois foi morta a tiros por policiais.

➡️ Portando duas facas, a criminosa matou a vice-presidente do Bank of América e também esfaqueou um homem de 68 anos, que ficou ferido, em um ataque deliberado na Times Square, a praça mais famosa dos Estados Unidos. Ela foi cercada por policiais após o crime, e morta com um tiro após avançar para cima deles ainda com as facas em mãos.

Ela foi identificada como Erin Piacenti e era vice-presidente do Bank of America, segundo o banco, que emitiu uma nota:

"Estamos chocados e profundamente entristecidos com a trágica perda de nossa colega. Ela era uma integrante valiosa da equipe e deixará muitas saudades. Nossos sentimentos estão com sua família e todos os seus entes queridos", afirmou o comunicado.

Piacenti, que era vice-presidente de seleção de negócios e conflitos de interesse do banco, morreu no hospital em decorrência dos ferimentos causados ​​pelas facadas, segundo a agência de notícias "Bloomberg News".

A vice-presidente do Banf of América Erin Piacenti. — Foto: Reprodução/ Redes sociais

Imagens capturadas por pessoas que passavam pela Times Square, em Nova York, registraram o momento em que policiais cercaram e atiraram contra a mulher que esfaqueou Piacenti e outro homem.

As imagens mostraram o momento em que policiais cercam a mulher, tentando detê-la ( veja no vídeo acima ).

Após cerca de quatro minutos na encruzilhada, a mulher levanta e roda os braços com as facas na mão. Em seguida, ela avança rapidamente em direção aos policiais enquanto movimenta as facas.

Os agentes usam armas de choque contra a mulher, mas ela continua avançando. Um deles saca então um revólver e dispara. Na sequência, a mulher cai no chão e é algemada. Segundo a polícia, ela morreu após ser baleada.

Mulher avança em direção a policiais na Times Square de Nova York com facas após esfaquear outras duas pessoas, em 31 de agosto de 2026. — Foto: Reprodução/ g1

👉 O ataque aconteceu perto de uma unidade do Departamento de Polícia de Nova York (NYPD), ao lado do One Times Square, prédio onde ocorre a tradicional descida da bola na festa de Ano Novo da cidade.

A polícia afirmou que a mulher retirou duas facas de uma sacola de compras e atacou primeiro um homem de 68 anos, atingido no abdômen. Em seguida, Piacenti também no abdômen. As duas vítimas foram levadas para um hospital.

Polícia de Nova York interditou área da Times Square após mulher esfaquear duas pessoas e ser baleada — Foto: Angela Weiss/AFP

Por causa da ocorrência, a polícia interditou parte da 7ª Avenida e orientou moradores e turistas a evitar a região. A área foi isolada enquanto agentes trabalhavam no local.

👉 A Times Square é uma das áreas mais conhecidas de Nova York e um dos principais pontos turísticos da cidade. A região é conhecida pelos grandes painéis luminosos, teatros da Broadway e lojas.

articles.title: Ventania com rajadas de até 93 km/h causa estragos no litoral de SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Ocorrências atingiram veículos, moradias e redes elétricas em cinco cidades nesta terça-feira (1º). Porto de Santos chegou a ficar fechado por causa do vento.
articles.summary: Santos, Mongaguá, Cubatão, Guarujá e São Vicente registraram ocorrências em razão das rajadas de vento. Ninguém ficou ferido, segundo os registros das equipes da Defesa Civil.
articles.body:
Uma forte ventania, com rajadas que chegaram a 93,41 km/h , derrubou ao menos 16 árvores em cinco cidades da Baixada Santista , no litoral de São Paulo, nesta terça-feira (1º). Santos , São Vicente , Mongaguá , Guarujá e Cubatão registraram ocorrências provocadas pelos ventos.

Além das árvores, foram registradas quedas de galhos, toldos e de um telhado. As ocorrências atingiram redes elétricas, veículos e moradias. Veja abaixo o balanço por cidade.

As prefeituras de Praia Grande, Peruíbe, Itanhaém e Bertioga foram procuradas pelo g1 e informaram que não havia registro de ocorrências atendidas pelas respectivas Defesas Civis até a última atualização desta reportagem.

São Vicente registrou queda de árvore na Rua Borges de Medeiros, no Jóquei Clube — Foto: Paulo Henrique

De acordo com a Prefeitura de Santos, o município acumulou 77,2 mm de chuva nas últimas 72 horas. Segundo a Praticagem de Santos, as rajadas de vento chegaram a 93,41 km/h, por volta de 0h20 . Às 9h15, o vento chegou a 75,9 km/h. Os morros permanecem em estado de observação.

O Porto de Santos ficou fechado entre 0h e 2h30 devido às condições do vento . Durante o período, um navio deixou de entrar no complexo portuário. Após a reabertura, as operações foram retomadas sem restrições.

Por causa das chuvas, houve alagamento na Avenida Nossa Senhora de Fátima, com situação mais crítica na altura da Rua Boris Kauffmann. Segundo a prefeitura, apenas a faixa da esquerda estava transitável nos dois sentidos.

Ao todo, foram registradas seis quedas de árvores na cidade até a última atualização desta reportagem. Segundo a prefeitura, equipes da Secretaria de Prefeituras Regionais (Sepref) foram acionadas para os atendimentos, com previsão de conclusão dos trabalhos até o fim do dia.

As ocorrências foram registradas nos seguintes locais:

Avenida Francisco Glicério com Rua Sergipe;

Rua Vergueiro Steidel com Almirante Cochrane;

Rua Particular Lélia com Epitácio Pessoa;

Rua Olintho Rodrigues Dantas com Comendador Martins;

Rua Vergueiro Steidel, 214, em imóvel particular.

A Prefeitura de São Vicente informou que registrou 42 mm de chuva nas últimas 24 horas.

A cidade teve um ponto de alagamento na Avenida Augusto Severo, próximo à Rua Armando Vitorio Bei. Segundo a administração municipal, porém, a via permanecia transitável.

Uma árvore caiu na Avenida Papa João Paulo II, na altura do km 3,5. Equipes municipais foram acionadas para remover a árvore e desobstruir a via.

Mongaguá registrou cinco quedas de árvores; duas atingiram veículos — Foto: Defesa Civil

Segundo a Prefeitura de Mongaguá, foram registradas rajadas de vento de aproximadamente 42 km/h.

A Defesa Civil atendeu cinco ocorrências de queda de árvores no bairro Vera Cruz, além da queda de dois toldos no Centro. Duas árvores atingiram veículos. Não houve registro de feridos.

Segundo a prefeitura, os ventos fortes contribuíram para as ocorrências. No caso das árvores, as condições anteriores das plantas também podem ter influenciado as quedas. Já os toldos podem ter se desprendido por causa das rajadas.

A Prefeitura de Guarujá informou que a Defesa Civil registrou a queda de duas árvores na região da Enseada. As rajadas chegaram a 67,70 km/h. Não houve vítimas.

Uma das árvores atingiu a rede elétrica. Segundo a prefeitura, a Defesa Civil aguardava a chegada da concessionária de energia para fazer a retirada. A outra árvore caiu dentro do terreno de uma residência.

A Defesa Civil de Cubatão informou que equipes municipais foram mobilizadas para atender ocorrências envolvendo a queda de duas árvores, um telhado e um galho.

Uma das árvores caiu sobre uma moradia na Rua Belarmino do Amaral, no Jardim São Francisco. A outra atingiu a rede elétrica na Avenida Joaquim Miguel, 374.

Outra rede elétrica foi atingida por um galho na Rua Marechal Deodoro, em frente à UME São Paulo, no Parque Fernando Jorge. A CPFL foi acionada para atender as duas ocorrências envolvendo a rede de energia.

Segundo a Prefeitura de Cubatão, as equipes também foram acionadas após a queda de um telhado em um imóvel na Rua 25 de Dezembro, na Vila Natal.

articles.title: A Miami man posed as the son of a 94-year-old woman and put himself on the title of her $625,000 home; 3 years after his arrest, he has been sentenced to 20 years in prison
articles.summary: US News: A Miami-Dade man was sentenced to 20 years in prison for exploiting a 94-year-old woman by pretending to be her son, draining her finances and putting.
articles.body: A Miami-Dade man was sentenced to 20 years in prison for exploiting a 94-year-old woman by pretending to be her son, draining her finances and putting himself on the title to her house. According to a report filed by the NBC 6 website, the Miami-Dade State Attorney’s Office said Wednesday that Alejandro Diaz Torriente, 67, was convicted in the financial exploitation case and sentenced. He will be on probation for 10 years after his prison sentence. According to reports, Diaz Torriente was arrested in 2023 by the State Attorney’s Office Elder and Vulnerable Adult Exploitation Task Force after a four-month investigation. Authorities said the victim had been living alone in her El Portal home, which she bought in 1980. But in 2021 she was declared legally incompetent, leaving her especially vulnerable to financial exploitation. Diaz Torriente had known the woman as a friend. Investigators said he began calling her "mom" and pretending to be her son during doctor's visits and other interactions at some point. Authorities later found a trail of financial transactions and property records showing he had defrauded the elderly woman.Social security payments redirectedInvestigators say the woman’s Social Security benefits were redirected to an unknown bank account. Diaz Torriente also allegedly opened bank accounts from which he withdrew approximately $20,000 in cash from the woman. The investigation went beyond the alleged theft of her money. Authorities said Diaz Torriente also targeted the woman’s house, which is worth about $625,000.Man charged with putting himself on home’s titleInvestigators found Diaz Torriente had filed a fraudulent deed adding himself as joint tenant with rights of survivorship on the woman’s El Portal property. The agreement would have afforded him substantial rights to the house and possibly entitled him to automatically inherit the property on the woman’s death. Diaz Torriente eventually took over the house and changed the locks, authorities said, further limiting the elderly woman’s access to her own home. The case highlighted that elderly and vulnerable adults can be targeted not only for their savings but also for valuable property.Prosecutor warns against“This case should serve as a warning to anyone who would try to exploit vulnerable older residents,” said Miami-Dade State Attorney Katherine Fernandez Rundle. “This case sends a clear message to those who seek to leave our elders destitute and discarded that we will not tolerate this type of heartless crime against our vulnerable residents,” Fernandez Rundle said in a statement Wednesday. Diaz Torriente will spend two decades in prison for the scheme and a decade on probation.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘My jaw physically dropped like a cartoon’: US woman summoned to court on wedding day in Rome
articles.summary: US News: A Kansas City bride has gone viral after receiving a jury duty summons for the same day as her wedding in Rome, more than 5,000 miles away.Katrina Bad.
articles.body: A Kansas City bride has gone viral after receiving a jury duty summons for the same day as her wedding in Rome, more than 5,000 miles away.Katrina Badowski, 35, received the summons on August 14, requiring her to report for a week of jury duty starting Monday — the day she was due to marry her fiancé, Billie Rodriguez, 42, in Italy.“My jaw physically dropped like a cartoon,” Badowski told KSHB outside the Wyandotte County District Court, recalling her reaction to seeing the date on the summons.Badowski, who said she had not been summoned for jury duty in more than a decade, shared a video of the notice on social media. Her post quickly went viral, drawing more than a million views on Instagram and TikTok.“The odds of you getting summoned for jury duty on your wedding day are low, but never zero,” she wrote, joking that “the government wants to be involved in my marriage SO BAD”.The summons initially left Badowski in a difficult situation. Kansas law allows courts to penalise people who fail to appear for jury duty without informing officials, with fines of up to USD 100 for each day missed and possible contempt of court charges.Despite the clash, Badowski said she would normally welcome the chance to serve on a jury.“I find it deeply ironic that I haven’t been summoned for jury duty in over a decade, as I would genuinely welcome the opportunity,” she told People.However, with flights, venues and vendors for the destination wedding already booked and paid for, attending jury duty was not possible.Badowski contacted court officials by email and was eventually excused from service. The court's response also included a congratulatory message: “Received and excused you from jury duty. Thank you and congratulations.”The unusual situation resonated with social media users, with several people sharing stories of jury duty coinciding with major life events.Badowski said she still hopes to fulfil her “jury duty dreams” someday. For now, her focus is on getting married in Italy.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Meet Jasmyn Blackburn, the kindergarten teacher making a case for dopamine dressing: ‘If I see something that’s colourful, sparkly, fun and makes me smile, I’ll wear it!’
articles.summary: Jasmyn Blackburn, aka Jazzy, 23, is living her dream life as a kindergarten teacher at a small school in Indiana. It’s everything she dreamed of: sequ.
articles.body: Jasmyn Blackburn, aka Jazzy, 23, is living her dream life as a kindergarten teacher at a small school in Indiana. It’s everything she dreamed of: sequins, sparkle and smiles, lots of them. On her first day as a teacher, she walked in wearing a sequined apple dress. That’s certainly not one of the immediate choices for most first-year teachers on opening day. But Jazzy wasn’t trying to disappear into the background. She was trying to show her five-year-olds that their teacher loved school and that she was going to make it fun!“I once heard the term ‘dopamine dressing’, and it immediately stuck with me,” she told People. “If I see something that’s colourful, sparkly, fun and makes me smile, I’ll wear it!”Taking dopamine dressing seriouslyBlackburn’s personal style is simple. She wears clothes that make her happy. And that’s exactly what dopamine dressing is all about. Initially, her colourful clothes impressed the kids. Soon, others started to notice too. Nine months into her teaching career, she had earned nearly 600,000 TikTok followers who tune in to watch her get dressed for work. Her clothes are simply eye-catching. Think colourful fabrics, glitter, sequins and a refusal to apologise for any of it!In fact, her love for colourful clothes goes back to her childhood. She was nicknamed ‘Snazzy Jazzy’ in first grade for her fun clothes. During her teenage years, she wanted to fit in, and that’s when she went for a ‘normal style’. But then she entered the teaching profession. And here, colourful dressing wasn’t a problem. The young kids appreciated her style more than anyone else.“Now that I’ve found my career in teaching, I feel like I’ve found the perfect profession that allows me to dress for my inner child again,” Blackburn said.Making teaching funBlackburn has a curated wardrobe for school. School-themed pieces dominate her collection, roughly 90 per cent, by her count. Teacher patches, sequined letters, apples, crayons and ABCs cover the garments hanging in what used to be a regular bedroom but is now her personal dressing room, painted entirely pink. “We actually have an entire room in our house that’s painted pink and serves as my closet and dressing room, so my wardrobe has definitely taken on a life of its own!” she said.Unlike during her teen days, showing up in colourful clothes at the kindergarten is no longer frowned upon. She could show up covered in sequins and school logos, and that is actually appropriate. More than that, it’s welcomed.“I love pieces that incorporate school themes because there aren’t many professions where you can show up to work covered in sequins, apples, crayons and ABCs, but in kindergarten, it just works!” she said.The unique shopping experienceBlackburn has her own strategy for shopping for the right pieces for school. Queen of Sparkles, Sparkle in Pink, ReallyRexBoutique and Depop are some of her popular shopping destinations. And the ‘Queen of the Classroom’ collection by Queens of Sparkles has to be her favourite.“Their pieces are definitely an investment, but the quality is amazing, and with how much I wear them, they end up being worth it for me,” she said.Her most expensive outfit, a Queen of Sparkles polka-dot set with sequined patches, retails for roughly $400 combined. Her first-day-of-school dress cost $39. “I think that’s a perfect example of how you absolutely don’t have to spend hundreds of dollars to find a fun, memorable piece that makes you feel amazing,” she said.Now she buys more strategically. Maybe one special piece per month, and that’s enough. Her collection is now large enough that she can mix and match and rotate outfits without repeating them often. “I just see something fun and figure out how to make it work!” she says.But this wasn’t always the case. In the beginning, she used to shop frequently, once every week. She does not have children, so the remaining money after paying the bills goes towards clothing. “Was saving it probably the more financially responsible choice? Yes. But fashion is something that genuinely makes me happy, and now I have a wardrobe I can continue wearing and styling for years,” she told the outlet.Thinking of building your personal wardrobe?Fashion has practically become Blackburn’s second name. So, if you were to ask her for some fashion advice on how to bring more personality into your work wardrobe, she suggests starting with what you already have. Experiment with the colours.“You also don’t need 50 statement pieces to start dressing more fun. Find a few special pieces that genuinely spark joy for you and build outfits around them,” she said.For her, fashion is rather about how one feels. “‘Fun’ fashion is whatever makes you happy. The whole point is finding pieces that make you excited to get dressed in the morning.”And for Blackburn, it’s her colourful clothes. “I love sharing the colourful outfits, but I think what I’m really sharing is joy. If someone can find a little bit of happiness in seeing how happy I am about my outfit, my classroom or my students, then that means so much more to me than any number of views or followers ever could. I want to make the world a little more colourful and a little more smiley, one short video at a time.”Looking for trusted parenting advice? articles.title: D4VD makes bombshell claim in Celeste Rivas case as her family fires back
articles.summary: US Streamers News: D4VD’s legal battle in the Celeste Rivas case has taken another dramatic turn after the singer made a major claim in court about his financial situati.
articles.body: D4VD’s legal battle in the Celeste Rivas case has taken another dramatic turn after the singer made a major claim in court about his financial situation. The development came as his high-profile legal team stepped away from the case and a public defender was appointed to represent him. However, Rivas’ family is strongly questioning the situation. Through their attorney, Patrick Steinfeld, the family has pointed to D4VD’s music success and business interests while demanding justice for Celeste. The latest development adds another layer to the closely watched case.D4VD makes bombshell financial claim as Celeste Rivas’ family reactsD4VD, whose legal name is David Anthony Burke, told the court that he was indigent, meaning he claimed he could not afford to pay for his own lawyers.Following that development, his powerful legal team, including attorney Blair Berk, withdrew from the case. The court then appointed the Los Angeles County Public Defender’s Office to handle his defense.D4VD’s former lawyers said they continue to support him and his defense. They also said they were grateful that the public defender’s office had taken over the case and that he now has a team of attorneys and investigators working for him.However, Celeste Rivas’ family has strongly challenged D4VD’s claim.Their attorney, Patrick Steinfeld, said the family was shocked to learn that Burke claimed to be indigent. He pointed to D4VD’s large music audience, saying the singer has more than 5 billion streams and around 16 million monthly listeners on one streaming platform.Steinfeld also pointed to three companies connected to D4VD, D4VD Entertainment, Skullrose Merchandising and Headspace Publishing.Celeste Rivas’ family questions D4VD’s finances amid legal battleSteinfeld argued that D4VD should not be considered unable to pay for his defense because his assets may be held through his companies.The attorney also referred to testimony from D4VD’s preliminary hearing. According to the statement, there were allegations that D4VD transferred assets to his mother and manager, Colleen Burke.The Rivas family attorney claimed this was an attempt to protect D4VD’s estate from a possible civil lawsuit and make it harder for Celeste’s family to access those assets.These are allegations from the family’s attorney, and they do not establish that D4VD illegally moved or hid money.The family said its main goal is to get justice for Celeste and see whoever is responsible face the full force of the law. They also thanked people who have continued to support their daughter.D4VD is facing serious charges in connection with the case, including murder, continuous sexual assault of a minor under 14 and unlawful mutilation of human remains, according to TMZ’s report.D4VD will now continue his case with the Los Angeles County Public Defender’s Office representing him. He is scheduled to return to court on October 19. Meanwhile, Celeste Rivas’ family continues to question his financial claims as the legal battle moves forward.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: He started washing dishes at 15 in a small Washington cafe; decades later Michael Mina had built a restaurant empire with more than 25 restaurants
articles.summary: US News: Michael Mina’s journey from a teenage dishwasher in rural Washington to the founder of a restaurant empire is a story shaped by hard work, curiosity a.
articles.body: Michael Mina’s journey from a teenage dishwasher in rural Washington to the founder of a restaurant empire is a story shaped by hard work, curiosity and a determination to learn. Born in Cairo, Egypt, and raised in Ellensburg, Washington, Mina discovered his passion for cooking while working at a small café at the age of 15. What began with washing dishes quickly became an obsession with the kitchen, eventually leading him to culinary school and some of America’s most celebrated restaurants. He would go on to help create the acclaimed San Francisco restaurant ‘Aqua’ before building ‘The Mina Group’ into a collection of chef-driven dining concepts across the United States and beyond. According to Visa, Mina had founded more than 25 restaurants worldwide by 2023. Yet behind all the awards and growing business was a young dishwasher who simply wanted to learn how to cook.How did washing dishes lead Michael towards the professional kitchenMina’s professional story began in Ellensburg when he was 15 years old. According to Visa, he started as a dishwasher at a small café in his hometown. However, his interest in the work quickly went beyond the sink. The café’s owner began teaching him how to cook, and Mina became increasingly absorbed by what he was learning. He recalled lying in bed thinking about cooking and arriving at work four hours early so that he could spend more time learning in the kitchen. Within three months, he was cooking full-time. By the age of 15, he had already decided that cooking was the career he wanted to pursue. The Culinary Institute of America(CIA) describes Mina’s early years as a period in which he worked as a dishwasher, bus boy and prep cook before gravitating fully towards the kitchen. His willingness to use his own time to learn more eventually convinced him that he wanted to become a chef.Culinary school as a turning point in Mina’s careerAfter finishing high school, Mina pursued his ambition of becoming a professional chef at the Culinary Institute of America in Hyde Park, New York. His parents initially had reservations about his decision to choose culinary school. They had hoped he might follow a more traditional professional path, but Mina remained committed to cooking. While studying at the CIA, he spent weekends working at ‘Aureole’ in New York City alongside chef ‘Charlie Palmer.’ The experience gave him valuable exposure to a demanding professional kitchen. After earning his degree, Mina worked with chef ‘George Morrone’ at the ‘Hotel Bel Air’ in Los Angeles. His next opportunity would prove particularly significant. Within six months of working with Morrone, the two chefs began developing the concept and menu for Aqua, a high-end seafood restaurant in San Francisco.Impact of Mina’s childhood in his approach towards foodAlthough Mina grew up in Washington state, his family’s roots remained an important part of his relationship with food. The CIA notes that he was born in Cairo and moved with his family to Ellensburg when he was two. At home, his mother cooked Middle Eastern dishes, and Mina has recalled learning from the spices and flavours that filled family meals. According to Eater, Mina’s childhood in rural Ellensburg also influenced his understanding of food and hospitality. He experienced the town very differently from San Francisco, which he first visited at the age of 13. Mina later described the city as a place where he felt a greater sense of belonging and where the sights, smells and diversity of its food culture made a lasting impression on him. Those different experiences would eventually become part of his culinary identity. His later work combined the flavours of his Egyptian background, memories of his upbringing in Washington and the polished techniques he developed during his professional training.How did ‘Aqua’ put Michael Mina on the culinary mapAqua opened in 1991 and quickly attracted attention. Mina initially worked as chef de cuisine before becoming executive chef in 1993, a position he held for almost a decade, according to the CIA. The Mina Group reports that he devoted himself to refining the menu and improving the guest experience while personally training the kitchen staff. His work at Aqua brought major recognition, including the ‘James Beard Foundation's Rising Star Chef of the Year’ award in 1997 and ‘Best Chef: California in 2002.’ Yet one of Mina’s proudest memories was not necessarily an award. According to Visa, the first time his parents visited Aqua stood out as the highlight of his career. Seeing what he had created helped demonstrate that his decision to become a chef had been the right one.How did one successful restaurant become a restaurant empireIn 2002, Mina left the Aqua Development Corporation and established ‘Mina Group’ with tennis star Andre Agassi, according to the CIA. The business soon began developing restaurant concepts across the country. The growth was driven by more than a desire to simply open as many restaurants as possible. Mina developed different concepts while maintaining a strong focus on food, service and the overall guest experience. The Mina Group describes the company as having more than 30 chef-driven concepts across the United States at present.Visa reported in 2023 that Mina had founded more than 25 restaurants around the world. His career had grown far beyond the small café where he had first washed dishes as a teenager. Along the way, Mina also learned that culinary talent alone was not enough to sustain a restaurant. He told Visa that he wished he had spent more time understanding the business side earlier in his career. He also learned the importance of building long-term relationships with guests, supporting employees and knowing when to rely on other people rather than trying to do everything himself. Today, Mina’s career reflects the journey of someone who entered a restaurant kitchen at 15 simply looking for work and emerged decades later as one of America's most successful chef-restaurateurs. His story suggests that sometimes a career begins not with a grand plan, but with the willingness to stay a little longer, work a little harder and keep learning.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Missiles from anywhere? Japan’s new warship packs 360-degree SPY-7 radar to hunt threats
articles.summary: International News: Japan is building a new generation of missile-defence warships equipped with powerful radar systems as it seeks to counter growing missile threats fro.
articles.body: Japan is building a new generation of missile-defence warships equipped with powerful radar systems as it seeks to counter growing missile threats from North Korea and the wider region.The two Aegis System Equipped Vessels (ASEVs) will use the AN/SPY-7 radar as their primary sensor, forming a key component of Tokyo’s integrated air and missile-defence network.According to The War Zone (TWZ), the first of the two warships is taking shape with its large SPY-7 radar arrays integrated into the mast. The radar, derived from the US Missile Defense Agency’s Long Range Discrimination Radar programme, is designed to detect, track and discriminate ballistic-missile threats.The programme comes as Japan faces an increasingly challenging security environment, particularly from North Korea’s repeated missile launches and advancing capabilities. Tokyo is also closely watching China’s expanding military and missile capabilities.Radar at the heart of Japan’s defence pushThe AN/SPY-7(V)1 radar is central to Japan’s new missile-defence vessels. Derived from the US Long Range Discrimination Radar programme, the system is designed to detect, track and discriminate ballistic missiles and other airborne threats before the Aegis combat system directs interceptors against them.Each ASEV will be equipped with four SPY-7 radar arrays, providing 360-degree coverage. Japan says the system offers significantly greater tracking capability than the older SPY-1 radar and can handle multiple ballistic-missile threats simultaneously.The radar has also demonstrated its ability to search, detect, identify, track and discriminate live targets. In March 2026, it underwent a test involving live-target tracking as part of Japan’s ASEV programme.Two ships built for missile warfareJapan began developing the ASEVs after abandoning its planned land-based Aegis Ashore missile-defence system. The ships are intended to provide Tokyo with a mobile and persistent sea-based ballistic-missile defence capability.The first vessel is scheduled to enter service in fiscal 2027, followed by the second in fiscal 2028. Both will combine the SPY-7 radar with the Aegis Weapon System.Each warship will feature 128 vertical launch system cells, providing a substantial magazine for interceptors such as the SM-3 Block IIA and SM-6. The vessels are also being designed with capacity for future weapons and upgrades.The combination of four SPY-7 radar arrays, the Aegis combat system and 128 missile cells is intended to allow each ship to detect, track and engage multiple missile and airborne threats.North Korea remains Tokyo’s key concernNorth Korea is a major driver of Japan’s push to strengthen its ballistic-missile defences. Tokyo says Pyongyang continues to conduct repeated missile launches while developing increasingly sophisticated systems.In August 2026, Japan said a North Korean missile travelled about 690 km before falling into the Sea of Japan. Tokyo described the launch as a threat to Japan and regional security.Japan’s FY2026 defence budget identifies improving the ability to detect and track increasingly diverse and complex threats, including missiles and aircraft, as a priority.China is another major concern for Tokyo. Japan’s 2026 defence white paper describes China as its “greatest strategic challenge” and says Beijing has rapidly expanded the scale and capabilities of its nuclear, missile, naval and air forces.With the ASEVs, Japan is therefore betting on a combination of powerful radar, Aegis technology and a large missile magazine to keep pace with an increasingly crowded and sophisticated missile threat environment.

articles.title: Oracle layoffs: The '6 am email' didn't come on September 1, and employees across US and India are now 'watching' Slack counts
articles.summary: Tech News News: At 6 am on September 1, thousands of Oracle employees checked their inboxes and found nothing. That silence is what the company's workforce is talking.
articles.body: At 6 am on September 1, thousands of Oracle employees checked their inboxes and found nothing. That silence is what the company's workforce is talking about now. The date had taken on a life of its own inside Oracle, not because the company announced anything, but because Business Insider reported in mid-August that managers had been asked to draw up lists of affected staff, with the aim of lowering payroll before Oracle's second fiscal quarter opened on September 1. The report, citing people familiar with the plans and an internal document, said reductions on some teams could run into double-digit percentages. Employees did the rest of the arithmetic themselves, drawing on the memory of March 31, when termination emails from "Oracle Leadership" landed at roughly 6 am local time and told recipients that the same day was their last working day.So instead of an announcement, there is a countdown that keeps resetting. On r/employeesOfOracle, a megathread pinned by moderators has become the closest thing to an internal newswire, with workers in Bengaluru, Mumbai and across the US posting hour by hour. Some are tracking the company's Slack member count like a stock ticker, 150,198, then 150,181, then 150,113, and arguing over whether the drift is layoffs or ordinary month-end attrition. One employee in India noted the count began dropping around 6.30 am and wondered whether the company had shifted to the start of the local workday instead. Others are trading rumours that the cuts have slipped to September 15, to line up with a scheduled townhall, or all the way to September 30. Oracle has declined to comment and has not confirmed any of it.Why the March 31 Oracle layoff email still sets the toneThe reason a date on a fiscal calendar carries this much dread is that employees have already seen the format. The March email was short and procedural: after careful consideration of business needs, the role had been eliminated as part of a broader organisational change, and today was the last working day. Severance would follow, but only after signing paperwork sent via DocuSign. Workers were asked to submit a personal email address quickly, because access to their Oracle machine, mail and files was about to be switched off.Roughly 10,000 positions went in that single wave, spanning the US, India, Canada and Mexico, and hitting Oracle Health, Cloud, Sales, Customer Success and NetSuite's India Development Centre. Employees said at the time there was no HR call and no manager conversation beforehand. Some units were gutted in one pass, with staff reporting that teams like RHS and SVOS saw reductions of at least 30%, and that senior engineers, architects and programme managers were among those let go. None of it, according to a senior Oracle manager who wrote about it publicly on LinkedIn, was performance-based.Oracle employees in India and the US are reading login pages for cluesWith no official word, staff have turned to whatever signals they can find. A recurring thread this week concerns a tool called Device Lock Automation, which several employees noticed had been provisioned to their accounts in Oracle's identity management portal in late August. One post claimed its presence meant you were on the list. Others pushed back, saying it appears to have gone out to everyone and only matters if an internal system flags a specific user, and that the intent is to lock machines as and when cuts happen. In Bengaluru's Fusion teams, workers noted that an unusual number of M4 and M6 managers had booked leave through September 1 and wondered whether the lists were already finalised.Practical questions are surfacing too. What does severance actually look like? In India, the earlier round broadly followed the N+2 formula, where N is years of service paid out in months, with unvested RSUs forfeited. In the US, one California based employee affected by the March cuts explained on the forum that remote workers generally fall outside WARN protection, since it attaches to a physical office location, leaving them with roughly 10 days on payroll rather than 60 days of pay and benefits. That distinction matters more than usual at a company where a large share of the remaining 141,000 staff work remotely.The numbers behind Oracle's fresh round of job cutsThe pressure is not hard to trace. Oracle's headcount fell by about 21,000, or 13%, in the fiscal year ended May 31, dropping from roughly 162,000 to 141,000, with around 49,000 of those left in the US. Restructuring charges hit $1.8 billion, up 391% from $374 million a year earlier, against a $2.1 billion cap set in the 10-K filed on June 22. That leaves about $300 million of headroom, so anything at the scale Business Insider described would either need to fit inside the remainder or push Oracle into a second new restructuring plan in three years.Capital expenditure reached $55.7 billion in FY2026, up from $21.2 billion, as Oracle built out data centres for customers including OpenAI. Free cash flow ran to negative $23.7 billion. The company raised $43 billion in debt and $5 billion in equity, and expects about $40 billion more this fiscal year. Interest expense alone climbed to $4.6 billion from $3.6 billion. TD Cowen estimated in January that cutting 20,000 to 30,000 roles could free up $8 billion to $10 billion in incremental free cash flow.Strong Oracle revenue is exactly what makes these layoffs stingThe business itself is growing. FY2026 revenue rose 17% to $67.4 billion, cloud infrastructure revenue grew 77%, and remaining performance obligations closed the year at $638 billion, up from $553 billion at the end of Q3. Oracle's own annual filing credits AI adoption for part of the headcount decline and warns that further reductions may follow as deployment grows. Investors are not sold either: the stock is down more than 20% this year, and shareholders sued in January over what Oracle said about the borrowing needed to service its $300 billion OpenAI commitment.For employees refreshing an inbox at 6 am, none of that is the point. The jobs are being lined up against a date on a fiscal calendar, and right now nobody outside Oracle's leadership seems to know which date it is.Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: Data Darbar: Trump backs server farm boom as protests grow in US
articles.summary: US News: TOI correspondent in Washington: US President Donald Trump has thrown his weight behind one of the most contentious aspects of America's artificial-in.
articles.body: TOI correspondent in Washington: US President Donald Trump has thrown his weight behind one of the most contentious aspects of America's artificial-intelligence boom, risking support of his own MAGA base by warning that communities which reject data centers will end up “backwards and poor.”In a Truth Social post that came amid growing opposition across the country to resource-intensive server farms, echoes of which are now being heard in India too, Trump argued that embracing data centers would mean jobs, lower taxes and prosperity.“The only reason that communities throughout the USA should not want Data Centers is if they want to end up being backwards and poor. If they want to be successful and rich, with far lower taxes and jobs all over the place, let Data Reign,” Trump posted, adding, “The good news is that there are plenty of other places that want them. If we kill the Golden Goose, you will only have yourselves to blame. China could not be happier with this anti Data Center movement.”Trump's intervention comes as the US confronts a striking paradox: the country is racing to build the physical infrastructure needed for AI and stay ahead of China just as public opposition to that infrastructure is becoming a major political force. The fight is no longer a niche zoning dispute; it is increasingly about who pays for AI, who gets its benefits, and who bears its environmental and social costs.The US is currently building hundreds of data centers, with one estimate pointing to more than 3000 operating facilities over the next decade. The biggest developers are the technology giants -- Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta and Oracle -- along with AI companies such as OpenAI and infrastructure specialists including QTS, Digital Realty, Equinix, CyrusOne and others.Training and operating frontier AI models requires enormous computing capacity, turning data centers into something closer to power-intensive industrial plants than traditional office infrastructure. While the industry maintains that data centers are the backbone of the AI economy, opponents are asking if citizens should surrender scarce water, electricity, land and tax revenue to build them.There is now growing opposition across the country to data centers, with at least 75 projects worth about $130 billion blocked or delayed in the first quarter of 2026 alone, according to Data Center Watch. A University of Pennsylvania Annenberg survey found in August that 61 per cent of Americans opposed new data centers in their communities, up from 49 per cent just four months earlier.Similar opposition is also brewing in India, with protests in Thane and in Visakhapatnam, where Google has planned a $15 billion AI data-center hub in partnership with the Adani group. The complaints are remarkably consistent: fears of higher electricity bills, water consumption, noise, air pollution, diesel backup generators, loss of farmland, tax concessions, strain on transmission networks and lack of local control.Resistance in the US is strongest in Virginia – just outside Washington DC – America's traditional “Data Center Alley,” with major protests erupting in Prince William County, where residents have opposed proposed campuses over land use, power and environmental concerns. In Wisconsin, opposition to Meta-linked plans has become a statewide political issue. Pennsylvania, Arizona, North Carolina, Georgia, Ohio, Nebraska, New Mexico and Texas have also seen local campaigns.Local activism has crossed party lines, with residents on both sides of the political divide objecting to secrecy, tax incentives, environmental effects and loss of local control. The UPenn survey shows opposition is bipartisan: 69 per cent among Democrats, 53 per cent among independents and 54 per cent among Republicans. The protests essentially pits a coalition of Big Tech and developers versus a shifting alliance of homeowners, farmers, environmentalists, and populist politicians.Trump's intervention has therefore put him somewhat at odds with parts of his own political constituency. “We’re about to see whether President Trump can sway those voters to support them, as he’s done on many issues before,” well-known pollster Frank Luntz noted, even as many Trump supporters expressed outrage on his support for data centers on his Truth Social platform.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Secretive, rushed, chaotic': Whistleblower flags risks in Trump's USPS ballot plan
articles.summary: US News: A whistleblower has warned that a new US Postal Service (USPS) system being developed to implement president Donald Trump's mail voting order could di.
articles.body: A whistleblower has warned that a new US Postal Service (USPS) system being developed to implement president Donald Trump's mail voting order could disrupt ballot deliveries to millions of Americans, raising fresh concerns over the timing and reliability of the system ahead of the November midterm elections.The disclosure, released on Tuesday by Democratic senator Richard Blumenthal, alleges that USPS has been developing the federal ballot mail portal at speed and with limited testing, despite an ongoing legal battle over Trump's executive order.The anonymous federal official, represented by the nonprofit Whistleblower Aid, described the project as "secretive, rushed, chaotic, and fundamentally flawed" and warned of a "catastrophic failure"."The apparently sloppy and rushed manner in which the federal ballot mail portal and supporting IT systems are being built poses significant risk," the whistleblower said, according to news agency AFP."Potentially millions of American voters may not receive their mail-in ballot this election cycle in a timely manner, or at all," the official added.Under the proposed system, states would upload lists of voters receiving mail ballots along with identifying barcodes to a new federal portal. Postal workers would then check samples from ballot batches against the information before accepting them for delivery.The whistleblower alleges that USPS has adopted a "zero-percent failure policy", under which an entire batch could be rejected if a sampled barcode fails to scan or does not match the federal system.That could mean a single error in a batch of thousands of ballots delaying delivery of the rest until the discrepancy is resolved and the batch is checked again.Blumenthal, the senior Democrat on a Senate investigations panel, accused the Postal Service of risking voters' access to the ballot and called on Postmaster General David Steiner to abandon the plan."The whistleblower's allegations make clear that USPS lacks the technical or operational capability needed to effectively implement the (order's) provisions in a way that safeguards every citizen's right to vote in the upcoming midterm elections," Blumenthal said."The Postal Service has designed a system to disenfranchise millions of Americans," he later told reporters, according to the Associated Press, adding, "This administration seems hell-bent on changing the framework on casting ballots in this country clearly for political reasons.”The White House has described the mail voting provisions as "commonsense measures" aimed at combating fraud.Trump's March executive order seeks tighter controls on mail voting, including new requirements involving voter verification and ballot envelopes.The policy has faced repeated court challenges. A federal judge in Massachusetts has temporarily blocked key parts of its implementation, while allowing USPS to continue developing the portal for states that voluntarily choose to use it. The administration has appealed.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In 2023, buyers paid $87,000 for a crumbling 1979 Michigan concrete dome with caved-in ceilings; after a total overhaul, the 2,457-sq-ft home is back for $499,900
articles.summary: US News: An eye-catching 1970s concrete dome home in Michigan that was once left to decay, with collapsed ceilings and damaged walls, has returned to the prope.
articles.body: An eye-catching 1970s concrete dome home in Michigan that was once left to decay, with collapsed ceilings and damaged walls, has returned to the property market after a major renovation. Located in Brighton, Michigan, the 2,457-square-foot home is now listed for $499,900. The sharp rise in value comes just three years after the current owners bought the badly damaged shell for $87,000 in 2023. Reporting by Realtor.com shows how the four-bedroom monolithic dome has been completely transformed while keeping its unusual shape and adding modern fixtures, eco-friendly materials and open living spaces.From structural decay to a modern sanctuaryBefore-and-after footage shared by local estate agent Meghan Zoll of Zoll Homes showed how badly the property had deteriorated before the renovation. The original white exterior had become dark brown because of years of weather damage and neglect. Inside, the rooms had suffered water damage, peeling paint, torn carpets and collapsed ceiling panels. After the renovation, the interior looks very different. The living area now has high ceilings, custom double front doors, round windows and skylights that bring more natural light into the dome. One of the home's main features is a two-storey living room centred around a sunken conversation pit and a wood-burning fireplace. Above the conversation pit, a circular staircase curves upwards to a loft-style second floor with the upper bedrooms. Listing agent Carie Peregord of Re/Max Edge praised the way the central design connects the different spaces in an interview with Realtor.com. "The feeling from the living room with the main fireplace and how the stairs go up the center of the dome is incredible," Peregord stated. "When you are in the upstairs bedrooms, it feels like you are really protected in a cozy bird's nest."Architectural history and custom fittingsThe property was originally built in 1979 by a local builder who specialised in concrete dome homes across Michigan. He built it as his own home. Because of its thick monolithic concrete shell, the house offers natural insulation. Listing materials say its geometric design provides strong energy efficiency, making it relatively easy and affordable to heat and cool during different seasons. "The concrete dome structure is energy-efficient and very easy to heat and cool," Peregord told Realtor.com. "Almost everyone who has been in it has fallen in love with it." The kitchen has custom curved cabinets designed to follow the home's sloping walls, along with concrete worktops, a farmhouse sink, stainless-steel appliances and a butler's pantry. Restoration workers also saved and restored the original Japanese floor tiles in the kitchen, combining the home's original details with modern improvements. Across the rest of the four-bedroom home, sustainable materials and reclaimed wood features have been added along with high-efficiency systems designed to reduce energy use.Rural surroundings with town convenienceThe property sits on a 1.15-acre fenced plot and backs onto woodland, while the General Motors Proving Ground campus is directly across the road. "They do testing of new vehicles there," Peregord noted to Realtor.com. "It's also close to downtown Milford, which is an artsy small town. What's nice is that you have everything 10 minutes from the property, yet you are in the country with deer walking through your backyard." Outside, the home has a large concrete patio at the rear, reached through sliding glass doors from the formal dining room. The property also includes garden areas and mature trees along its boundaries. Peregord said the home's unusual character could attract buyers looking for something different from typical suburban houses. "It's such a vibey house," Peregord said. "And it's so close to everything you need, but it feels like you are in the middle of nowhere." The real estate agency said interest in the property has mainly come from artistic buyers, people interested in energy-efficient living and buyers looking for unusual architectural designs.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Germany fingers Moscow for airport drone, shuts two Russian bodies
articles.summary: The German government believes that the failed attack with an explosive-laden drone at Leipzig airport last month was carried out on behalf of Russia, Interi...
articles.body:
The German government believes that the failed attack with an explosive-laden drone at Leipzig airport last month was carried out on behalf of Russia, Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said on Tuesday, with the government in Berlin shuttering two Russian bodies in response.

Dobrindt told reporters in Berlin that police investigations, patterns of criminal activity and intelligence findings point to Russian responsibility for the attempted attack on the airport.

The minister said the technology found at the scene and the interplay of individual elements had to be described as professional, and indicated a high degree of technical expertise and considerable organizational effort in the planning and execution of the attack.

"The final execution of the attempted attack can be attributed to the area of low-level agents," he said, adding: "Let me make this clear: We are not at war, but we are a daily target of hybrid warfare."

The Russian consulate general in Bonn is to be closed on September 18, and the lease for the Russian House, a Russian cultural institution in the heart of Berlin, will be terminated, Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said.

Speculation had been rife for weeks that Moscow might be behind the August 4 incident, but Berlin has taken until now to officially identify a suspect, citing lengthy negotiations.

A drone fitted with explosives and a detonation mechanism was discovered on the evening of August 4 in the security zone of Leipzig/Halle Airport, between Ukrainian cargo aircraft, prompting a temporary halt to flights.

articles.title: River water smashed into tunnel and chased me for 20 minutes, Nepal worker tells BBC
articles.summary: Major efforts to rescue hydropower workers continue as Nepal's death toll exceeds 1,000.
articles.body:
Pemba Dundu Tamang tells the BBC how he discovered some of his colleagues were missing after he escaped a flooded tunnel

Nepalese hydropower workers have told the BBC about the catastrophic moment water from the Trishuli River crashed into their tunnel as the region was inundated by deadly flash floods last week.

It started with a sudden, strong gust of air, says Pemba Dundu Tamang, whose team of about 30 was constructing the tunnel's concrete lining.

The blast of wind sent plywood flying through the air and dislodged heavy machinery. Just outside, houses had already been swept away.

"I ran towards the tunnel entrance," he said. "The water was chasing behind me and I was running ahead of it."

Tamang lost several family members who were at home at the time. Nepal's death toll has exceeded 1,000 after last week's devastating floods, and officials say about 4,000 are missing.

A number of the missing - potentially in the hundreds - are labourers like Tamang, working in a vast network of tunnels at hydropower sites along the river. Engineers have been pumping air into these tunnels as part of a huge rescue operation.

"We are focused on search-and-rescue efforts at the tunnels, our work is continuing," Nepal Army spokesman Raja Ram Basnet told AFP news agency.

"Our soldiers are also deployed to collect bodies and prevent the spread of disease."

Tamang says he ran for about 20 minutes to flee the violent deluge, which followed him uphill.

"I was almost unconscious with shock. I could not think clearly."

His colleague, Itha Ghale, says the powerful gust of air almost blew them away as they sprinted.

Over 99% of the electricity generated in Nepal comes from hydropower, and Tamang and Ghale had been working at a major production site helping to build the Upper Trishuli 3B Hydropower Project.

The plant, which was due to open next year, was designed to re-use water from a hydroelectric plant further upstream to generate additional electricity for Nepal's national grid.

There were several different teams operating there - and Tamang says the one operating the large tunnel-lining machine was the last to come out.

But soon afterwards came a crushing realisation.

"I could see where my house should have been. There was nothing left. That was when I realised everything was gone."

Six of Tamang's relatives - his mother, elder brother and sister-in-law and three of their children - are gone, he said. They were at home on the riverside when the floods hit.

Only his wife, son and one nephew survived.

"I feel life is meaningless now. Surviving feels miserable. I do not know where to eat or where to go," Tamang says.

"The dead are at peace. It is those of us who survived who suffer."

Ghale, who lost eight members of his family, says he does not know why he survived. "Perhaps it was not my fate to die."

The eight family members include his mother and eldest daughter. His three sons and wife survived.

Tamang dreads what the future may bring, especially if these hydropower projects are shut down. "If things continue like this, we will go hungry. Sometimes I feel it would have been better not to survive."

Tamang ultimately managed to take refuge with a few others in the village of Shanti Bazar for two days until the army came to rescue them.

He estimates about 50 to 60 workers were able to escape the tunnel alongside him.

He says more people could have been saved if proper resources had been in place.

This is echoed by a new report which says there was evidence of growing instability around the glacier in the days before the disaster - and that better early warning systems could have saved lives.

Satellite images suggest the glacier surface was moving faster, meltwater was turning brown and a crack was developing in the surrounding rock, according to experts from the Asian Mountain Academic Alliance, the Stimson Centre and China's Institute of Mountain Hazards and Environment.

These are all possible signs the mountainside was becoming unstable.

The avalanche itself moved too fast for conventional warnings to help those closest to it, the scientists say.

But further downstream, where the flood took 10 minutes or more to arrive, they say a comprehensive warning system could potentially have saved a significant number of lives.

Right now, however, specialists from China, India and Nepal are continuing to use excavators and heavy machinery to blast through debris from the hydropower projects to try to reach workers still trapped at several hydropower sites.

"There are probably still some survivors inside. I would be happy if they were rescued quickly," Tamang says.

"I know many people who are still trapped there."

Additional reporting by Justin Rowlatt, climate editor

articles.title: Nepal floods bring 'unusual' fish to Bihar, govt warns people not to eat or sell them
articles.summary: India News: BETTIAH: Unidentified and unusual fish swept into the Gandak river and its floodplains by floodwaters from Nepal have prompted the Bihar govt to issue.
articles.body: BETTIAH: Unidentified and unusual fish swept into the Gandak river and its floodplains by floodwaters from Nepal have prompted the Bihar govt to issue a safety advisory, asking residents of West Champaran and Gopalganj not to consume or trade in such fish until their identity and safety are confirmed.The fisheries division of the dairy, fisheries and animal resources department issued the caution on Tuesday after unusual fish were found in local water bodies and low-lying areas across the flood-hit Gandak basin.Floodwaters from Nepal have entered the Gandak system, inundating several areas of West Champaran and Gopalganj. The department said fish can be swept away from ponds, rivers and other water bodies during floods and carried over considerable distances. During this movement, they may come into contact with contaminated drains, dead animals and other pollutants, raising the risk of contamination by bacteria, viruses and fungi.“Do not consume any unidentified or unusual-looking fish. Until confirmation by the concerned department, an unfamiliar fish should not be considered fit for consumption,” the advisory said.Residents have also been asked not to buy or sell unfamiliar fish caught from floodwaters or assume an unusual-looking species is safe merely because it resembles a commonly eaten fish. Anyone developing vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, dizziness or breathing difficulty after consuming such fish has been advised to seek immediate medical attention.Wildlife Trust of India director Sameer Kumar Sinha said most fish swept into the Gandak in Bihar following the Nepal floods are believed to be ‘Bagarius bagarius’, commonly known as the goonch catfish and locally called “Gochita”.He said the large freshwater catfish is found in fast-flowing rivers of India, Nepal and parts of Southeast Asia. The carnivorous species feeds on smaller fish, crabs and other aquatic organisms and often hides among rocks in deep stretches with strong currents.Sinha said local communities consume the fish, but it spoils quickly after death and may pose health risks if eaten after deterioration. He urged people to follow the Bihar govt advisory and exercise caution. The species is listed by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) as threatened.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: More than 40 Tennessee tiny-home owners are seeking $5 million in a 'zombie HOA' lawsuit, alleging nearly 80% of the HOA budget went to a lawn care company owned by the developer
articles.summary: US News: More than 40 homeowners in three tiny-home communities in Tennessee are taking legal action against developer Claude 'Chip' Hayes III, accusing him of.
articles.body: More than 40 homeowners in three tiny-home communities in Tennessee are taking legal action against developer Claude 'Chip' Hayes III, accusing him of retaining control of their homeowners associations (HOAs) and mismanaging association funds. They are seeking $5 million in damages, along with control over HOA funds and records.The dispute centres on three developments including the Retreat at Deer Lick Falls, the Retreat at Sunset Bluff and Water’s Edge, Realtor.com reported. Residents there say Hayes continued to control their HOAs beyond the period allowed under the communities’ governing documents. They called it a 'zombie HOA', where a developer remains in control after residents are expected to take over.Hayes’ business model involved selling land to residents, developing roads and offering community amenities. Buyers could choose from several tiny-home models and either live in their homes or rent them as holiday properties through a property management service run by the developer. Residents also paid fees to an HOA that Hayes managed.Homeowners say problems emerged over the way the communities were managed. They have raised concerns about HOA finances, promised amenities, building work and restrictions on the contractors they could use.The legal fight began more than two years ago when residents of the Retreat at Deer Lick Falls sued Hayes, claiming he had failed to hand over control of the HOA and had mismanaged its funds. The dispute later expanded to include homeowners at Water’s Edge and Sunset Bluff.Developer kept control The governing documents for the developments gave Hayes control of the HOAs for a specific period while the communities were being built. This included control over builders, common areas, amenities and other association matters.According to the communities’ covenants, conditions and restrictions, Hayes was supposed to give up control either five years after the first lot was sold to a non-developer or once 75% of the lots had been sold to non-developers, whichever came first.Residents at Deer Lick Falls argue that this meant Hayes should have given up control in 2021. They allege he extended his control by adding more property to the Deer Lick community and arguing that the expansion justified keeping control of the HOA.Residents sued him in 2024 seeking control of the HOA. Homeowners at Water’s Edge later joined the legal dispute, alleging that property taxes on common areas went unpaid for more than two years and that the properties were at risk of a tax sale.They also accused the developer-controlled HOA of failing to provide proper financial records and entering transactions that benefited the developer at homeowners’ expense.The dispute escalated again in 2026 at Sunset Bluff. Hayes sought a temporary restraining order after learning that residents planned to hold a meeting to vote on taking control of the HOA.Residents still voted overwhelmingly to remove Hayes from control and elected their own board of directors. The new board then changed several policies, including allowing homeowners to choose their own property managers rather than being required to use the developer’s rental management company.HOA money misusedThe Sunset Bluff residents then filed a counterclaim against Hayes and his companies. In July, 40 residents signed on to a lawsuit accusing Hayes of self-dealing, breaching his fiduciary duties, overcharging for services and illegally retaining control of the community’s finances. Homeowners are seeking $5 million in damages.A major part of their complaint concerns HOA spending. The lawsuit alleges that nearly 80% of the entire HOA budget at Sunset Bluff was spent on lawn care services. Residents also claim those contracts were awarded to another company owned by Hayes.The lawsuit also alleges that HOA money from Sunset Bluff was used to pay for the development of a separate project, the Retreat at Deer Lick Falls Phase Two.Homeowners further claim that they had to pay for the removal of dozens of dead trees damaged during construction, despite already paying HOA dues. The complaint also alleges that Hayes tried to charge residents extra for using a community building that had been built using HOA funds.Hayes has largely remained silent about the lawsuits. Earlier this month, however, he told the Moore County Observer that former business partners and homeowners fighting for control had made it difficult to operate the retreats. He also blamed legal expenses for his inability to complete some of the amenities that had been promised to residents.“I should have folded up and walked away a long time ago. Anybody else would have. But I don’t want to leave the customers damaged in this. This is something that I love and believe in,” he said, as quoted by Realtor.com.Amenities not deliveredGregg Boling, who bought a lot at Water’s Edge in 2021, said he had planned to build a holiday home for himself and his family. He said he chose the property because Hayes had told him there would not be another property across from it and that an adjacent lot would become a community clubhouse with a saltwater pool. “The pool was always a part of the selling process for us,” Boling said.The pool was never completed, according to him. A lawsuit filed by the pool’s original installer alleged that Hayes failed to properly grade the site, causing water runoff problems and structural damage.Water’s Edge residents have also alleged that other advertised amenities, including hiking trails, kayak access, pools, a pool house and a cabana, were not completed. The saltwater pool remains listed on the community’s website as “coming soon”.Boling also questioned the quality of construction and the contractors residents were expected to use. After a contract dispute with builder Michael Weidenhamer, whom Hayes fired in 2022, Hayes circulated a list of contractors who were banned from working for residents.Boling said he later discovered that his water main had been installed almost 30 inches below the surface. During a particularly cold winter, he said he had to dig 44 inches down to locate it and used a metal detector borrowed from a friend.Residents describe more problems with their propertiesLinda Ranz, who owns properties in both Water’s Edge and Sunset Bluff, said she bought two Water’s Edge lots intending to build homes for herself and her daughter. Ranz said the land did not initially have waterfront access, but Hayes told her he would dredge part of Big Fiery Gizzard Creek to provide it. That never happened.“For two years, I was told, ‘Yeah, there's going to be water. He's going to dredge that.’” Ranz said she eventually asked when the dredging would happen and was told, “oh, never.”Ranz has raised other concerns about roads, septic systems and drainage. She said Hayes built a large drainage ditch through the middle of her property without her permission, forcing her to spend another $2,500 on a survey so she could create a driveway to a second house.At Sunset Bluff, she said she is paying $120 a month in HOA fees for each of her four lots, despite having no home or lawn on them. She said she does not know where the money is going.Despite the lawsuits, Hayes continues to pursue new development projects. Earlier this month, he appeared before the Metro Board of Zoning Appeals seeking permission to build a 17-acre RV park and campground at the Retreat at Whiskey Creek.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
